lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: constructing a tangent line from a point outside a circle
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: constructing a tangent line from a point outside a circle

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read the example first. You are not expected to know this yet.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Try each one. If you get stuck, write what you do know and move on.

items.prompt: A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±5, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 6. Write its equation.
Compare a cone and a cylinder with the same base and height. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.
They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 5 and centre O. A point P lies 13 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 8.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 12.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 5; the tangent length is 12.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 12.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±3, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 10. Write its equation.
A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±13, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 24. Write its equation.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Show what you can do so far. This sets the starting point, not a grade.

items.prompt: Compare a sphere of radius r and a cylinder of radius r and height 2r with two cones removed. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.
The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 7 and centre O. A point P lies 25 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 24.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 24.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 18.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 7; the tangent length is 24.
